1	# Status
2	
3	**Updated:** 2026-10-28
4	
5	Core extraction, resolver, CLI, NAPI binding, and Vite plugin all work and are fully tested. Config file loading, watch mode (including rebuilds on config changes and polling with `ensure_fresh`), plugin architecture, TOON token-optimized output format, JSON schema export, and bounded atomic DTS caching are implemented and verified.
6	
7	**Types from other packages.** Imports resolve to any file under a source directory, `.d.ts` included, so a monorepo whose packages are all source directories resolves across them. By default the declarations those names point to are loaded (ADR 0010): a prop typed by an installed package resolves. `--no-load-dependencies` (config, NAPI and Vite `loadDependencies: false`) reads only `@types/react` and TypeScript's own lib files from `node_modules`, and then a prop whose type comes from any other installed package stays a named reference with an `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT` warning. Checked against RDT on five installed repos, loading reports far more of RDT's props and changes 11 matching types in 59,000. Chakra, the worst case, costs about 220 ms and 330 MiB against 50 ms and 100 MiB without (`docs/performance.md`).
8	
9	## Numbers
10	
11	- Rust tests (`cargo nextest` across the workspace, plus the NAPI binding tests) and vitest (unit with a mocked binding, integration against the real native binding), all green in CI
12	- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` clean with `unsafe_code = "deny"` enforced workspace-wide
13	- 20 real-world fixture libraries validated against `react-docgen-typescript` (shadcn, Radix, MUI, Chakra, Mantine, React Aria, antd, ariakit, ark-ui, base-ui, blueprint, day-picker, fluentui, headlessui, panda, react-final-form, react-resizable-panels, storybook-emotion, tanstack-table, zendesk-garden — see `rdt-coverage.md`)
14	- **Recall** against `react-docgen-typescript` with dependencies installed and loaded (`docs/measurement.md`, 2026-10-23): share of RDT's non-React props reported Mantine 99.7%, Chakra 98.6%, shadcn/ui 39.5%, Ant Design 80.3%, react-spectrum 99.7%.
15	- **Precision** per detection rule (`docs/precision.md`, 2026-10-21): 1 component that isn't one in 154 sampled, `functionDeclaration` 96% and every other rule 100%. 25 samples per rule can't yet establish the 95% gate.
16	- **Speed** on five pinned public corpora (`docs/performance.md`, 2026-10-22): 34 to 81 ms wall time and 66 to 153 MB peak RSS for 41 to 490 kLOC, 17 to 39 times faster than `react-docgen-typescript` on the same files. No pull-request gate enforces it: a weekly workflow records speed, memory and recall against RDT and react-docgen and opens an issue on a worsening, and `just bench` compares a branch with `main` locally (`docs/measurement.md`).
17	
18	## Features and improvements
19	
20	- **`htmlAttributes` defaults to `full`** — every attribute `@types/react` declares is listed, `ref` for `forwardRef` and `ComponentProps<"div">` props; `curated` is an opt-in compact mode. Costs against the old default: wall time +9 to +31%, peak RSS +12 to +37%, canonical JSON +42 to +105%.
21	- **Testing Stack** — `cargo-nextest` process runner, `rstest` parameterized spec tables, `insta` snapshots, and `trycmd` executable Markdown CLI specs.
22	- **Plugin system** (`DocgenPlugin` / `PluginRegistry`) — Extensible AST and component resolution hooks in `crates/core/src/plugin.rs`.
23	- **TOON output format** (`--format toon` / `toon.rs`) — Token-optimized format for LLM agents, cutting context window token usage by ~65-75%.
24	- **JSON schema export** (`caliper-docgen schema`) — Machine-readable Draft-07 JSON Schema export for component metadata validation.
25	- **Atomic & Bounded DTS cache** (`cache.rs`) — Atomic temp-file swap writes, dirty flag tracking, and 5,000 entry eviction cap. Keyed by content hash, and discarded whenever the build that wrote it differs.
26	- **Lazy sessions** (ADR 0016) — `WatchSession::lazy` parses and indexes every file and resolves a component when a request names it; the Storybook addon uses it by default (NAPI `lazy`, off by default). Each answer equals the batch extraction's for the same key. Numbers in `docs/performance.md`.
27	- **Dependency declarations loaded by default** (ADR 0010) — a prop typed by an installed package resolves; `--no-load-dependencies` turns it off.
28	- **Strict Safe Rust** — `unsafe_code = "deny"` via `[workspace.lints]`, active across all three crates (`core`, `cli`, `binding`) — none currently use `unsafe`, including the NAPI FFI boundary (napi-rs's `#[napi]` macros generate the glue without user-visible `unsafe`).
29	
30	## Known gaps that won't get fixed without a type checker
31	
32	See the "Known gaps summary" table in `rdt-coverage.md` for the full, maintained list. The short version: conditional types that need inference (`infer`, an unbound generic), mapped types over an unbound generic, and a couple of `@emotion/styled`-specific call shapes all need real type inference OXC deliberately doesn't do. Not bugs. A conditional, indexed access or mapped type whose operands are known is evaluated (`resolver/evaluate.rs`).
33	
34	An opt-in TypeScript 7 semantic backend is implemented as slice 1 (ADR 0006, ADR 0007), experimental and off by default: `extract --experimental-semantic-types`, see `type-checker-integration.md`. Accuracy is verified against real RDT — 0 missing/extra props on 13 hand-picked components, and re-verified on `7.1.0-beta` against the full 44-file fixture corpus (5,508/5,522 `required` matches, 5,266/5,522 type-string matches; the gap is explained noise, not a resolver bug) — and the RDT oracle that comparison depends on now runs on its own `typescript@6` install, separate from the semantic probe's `typescript@7.1.0-beta`. TypeScript 7.1's checker also runs, test-only, as an oracle for structural prop types (`docs/measurement.md`). A session can also ask a warm checker for just the component a story requests (`semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`, ADR 0022): the first answer waits up to `semanticWaitMs` (default 150) and takes the structural props if the checker is slower, and the checker's late answer is kept for the next request. It needs `typescript@7.1.0-beta` (the pinned version) or `tscPath`, and is experimental and off by default. A missing, crashed or timed-out `tsc` falls back to the structural result with one warning; the open lifecycle items are in `type-checker-integration.md`'s Gates table.
35	
36	## Experiments that didn't pan out
37	
38	**Confidence routing (2026-10-25).** The idea: score each component's risk of wrong or missing props from Caliper's own output, and ask the TypeScript 7.1 checker only about the risky ones. Measured against the checker on 518,268 shared props over the five corpora and the fixtures, routing 10% of components caught 23% of the props only the checker reports with the existing warning rule (a component with a degrade warning or error), against 3% for a smoothed table and 6% for a logistic model. At a 20% budget neither model caught the one prop the oracle marks `wrong`. Most of the checker-only props were Next's ambient augmentation (1,154 of 1,182 on shadcn) or false component matches, which a score of structural risk can't learn. So no score ships: warnings stay the signal, and on-demand checker use asks about the requested component instead of predicting. The script was deleted; the method is the oracle in `docs/measurement.md` plus the numbers above.
39	
40	## Where to look next
41	
42	- **Open gaps** → `edge-cases.md` — the gaps still open. Add one when you find a gap you aren't fixing now; delete it when you fix it.
43	- **What broke and why, historically** → `rdt-coverage.md` — every bug found during real-library validation, root cause, and the fix. Keep this updated; it's the project's memory.
44	- **Why a hard-to-reverse decision was made** → `docs/adr/` — OXC over the TypeScript compiler, manual serde for `PropType`, positional msgpack encoding, panic containment, the TypeScript 7 semantic backend. Write a new one when you make a decision like these (see `docs/adr/README.md`).
45	- **How the pipeline fits together** → `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (moved from `.claude/semantic-model/` so every coding agent can read it, not just Claude Code — `AGENTS.md` is now this repo's shared instructions file, with per-tool mirrors under `.codex/`, `.cursor/`, `.gemini/`, `.github/`, `.opencode/`).
46	- **Setup, testing, code style, commit conventions** → `CONTRIBUTING.md`
47	- **Migrating from react-docgen-typescript** → `MIGRATING.md`

Accuracy is verified against real RDT — 0 missing/extra props on 13 hand-picked components, and re-verified on `7.1.0-beta` against the full 44-file fixture corpus (5,508/5,522 `required` matches, 5,266/5,522 type-string matches; the gap is explained noise, not a resolver bug) — and the RDT oracle that comparison depends on now runs on its own `typescript@6` install, separate from the semantic probe's `typescript@7.1.0-beta`. TypeScript 7.1's checker also runs, test-only, as an oracle for structural prop types (`docs/measurement.md`). A session can also ask a warm checker for just the component a story requests (`semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`, ADR 0022): the first answer waits up to `semanticWaitMs` (default 150) and takes the structural props if the checker is slower, and the checker's late answer is kept for the next request. It needs `typescript@7.1.0-beta` (the pinned version) or `tscPath`, and is experimental and off by default. A missing, crashed or timed-out `tsc` falls back to the structural result with one warning; the open lifecycle items are in `type-checker-integration.md`'s Gates table.
35	
36	## Experiments that didn't pan out
37	
38	**Confidence routing (2026-10-25).** The idea: score each component's risk of wrong or missing props from Caliper's own output, and ask the TypeScript 7.1 checker only about the risky ones. Measured against the checker on 518,268 shared props over the five corpora and the fixtures, routing 10% of components caught 23% of the props only the checker reports with the existing warning rule (a component with a degrade warning or error), against 3% for a smoothed table and 6% for a logistic model. At a 20% budget neither model caught the one prop the oracle marks `wrong`. Most of the checker-only props were Next's ambient augmentation (1,154 of 1,182 on shadcn) or false component matches, which a score of structural risk can't learn. So no score ships: warnings stay the signal, and on-demand checker use asks about the requested component instead of predicting. The script was deleted; the method is the oracle in `docs/measurement.md` plus the numbers above.
39	
40	## Where to look next
41	
42	- **Open gaps** → `edge-cases.md` — the gaps still open. Add one when you find a gap you aren't fixing now; delete it when you fix it.
43	- **What broke and why, historically** → `rdt-coverage.md` — every bug found during real-library validation, root cause, and the fix. Keep this updated; it's the project's memory.
44	- **Why a hard-to-reverse decision was made** → `docs/adr/` — OXC over the TypeScript compiler, manual serde for `PropType`, positional msgpack encoding, panic containment, the TypeScript 7 semantic backend. Write a new one when you make a decision like these (see `docs/adr/README.md`).
45	- **How the pipeline fits together** → `ARCHITECTURE.md`, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (moved from `.claude/semantic-model/` so every coding agent can read it, not just Claude Code — `AGENTS.md` is now this repo's shared instructions file, with per-tool mirrors under `.codex/`, `.cursor/`, `.gemini/`, `.github/`, `.opencode/`).
46	- **Setup, testing, code style, commit conventions** → `CONTRIBUTING.md`
47	- **Migrating from react-docgen-typescript** → `MIGRATING.md`

# Edge cases and known gaps

Gaps that are still open. The 2026-08-04 audit that this file used to record (crash and hang risks, silent data loss, silent wrong output; 43 fixes) has landed; its findings are in git history (`git log --follow docs/edge-cases.md`) and each fix has a regression test. Bugs found by real-library validation are in `rdt-coverage.md`. Type-inference gaps are in `type-checker-integration.md`.

Add an entry when you find a gap you are not fixing now. Delete it when you fix it.

## Detection

- Wrapper calls with no type argument are not recognized: `createIconLoader('x')`, `lazy(() => import(...))`, `createIcon({...})`. Reading the props needs the call's return type, which the structural path doesn't have. The opt-in TypeScript backend (ADR 0006) can.
- Some components are reported under a different name than `react-docgen-typescript` uses: `displayName` assignments, and compound members such as `Tabs.List`.

## Resolution

- Mapped types, conditional types and indexed access over an unbound generic, and `@emotion/styled`'s two-argument overload, need real type inference. They degrade to `Opaque` with a diagnostic and, where possible, a `composes` entry. See `type-checker-integration.md`.
- Ambient globals (`lib.dom.d.ts` and the like) are looked up from `options.src_dirs.first()` only (`pipeline/mod.rs`, `pipeline/revision.rs`). If the first source directory can't resolve `typescript` but a later one could, ambient lookups return nothing for the whole run. Untested against a real multi-root config.

## Output

- TOON is lossy on purpose: unions and intersections print at most 4 members, literal unions at most 6, each followed by `...(+N)`. The module doc of `toon.rs` doesn't say so.

1	# Caliper: plan for the next trails (written 2026-11-02)
2	
3	Read this whole file first. It is the agreed plan from a long planning session; the user approved the recommendations in "Decisions". Nothing in it has been created yet: no trail, no branch, no PR.
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	What we care about, in order: (1) types that are accurate for Storybook's use and usable by in-process agents (monokl, no shell-out); (2) a comparison with RDT and react-docgen that is honest and repeatable; (3) speed, without breaking features; (4) a release flow that publishes GitHub Releases. Parity with RDT is a means, not the goal: the TypeScript 7.1 checker is the ground truth (it is also what Storybook's own component meta uses).
8	
9	## Where we are (main at 2daef927 when written)
10	
11	Merged this week: schema v4 (#266), detection by shape (#267, #270), on-demand checker hardening (#268), layer `members` and weekly recall columns (#271, #278), Chakra NonNullable (#272), terminal React builtins (#273), module augmentation (#274), Pick/keyof/union (#277). The release PR #269 merged; release run 41485334016 was in flight (do not edit `.github/workflows/release.yml` or `callisto.toml` until it ends).
12	
13	Weekly records (artifacts: weekly.json, weekly.md; `gh run download <id>` is read-only):
14	
15	| Run | Meaning |
16	| --- | --- |
17	| 41159666463 | baseline, main 240a61c9 |
18	| 41459968910 | Monday scheduled run, before the merges, main e2064d23 |
19	| 41479003541 | after the merges, main 53970b80 |
20	
21	Recall vs RDT (components / own flat / own with layers / @types/react), baseline to latest: mantine 85.9/100/-/99.2 to 89.1/100/100/99.6; chakra 79.4/100/-/99.4 to 92.5/100/100/99.4; shadcn 95.2/49.7/-/97.1 to 96.5/58.2/99.6/99.6; antd 64.0/86.4/-/91.9 to 79.7/86.4/99.3/99.1; spectrum 76.2/99.4/-/98.3 to 97.6/99.5/99.5/98.3. Component jumps come mostly from the harness (#275 excludes non-components and pairs exports), not from detection. Per-run RSS is now real (shadcn 334 MiB; the old 1,593 MiB was a measurement artifact).
22	
23	Speed vs RDT (CI): 17x to 58x faster, 2.6x to 6.8x less memory.
24	
25	Oracle (TS 7.1 checker, agree / wrong): mantine 90.9/0.00, chakra 100/0.00, shadcn 90.1/0.08, antd 93.1/0.00, spectrum 83.8/1.09 (new since baseline; present on the Monday run, so v4 or detection work, not the latest merges; cause not yet investigated).
26	
27	Regression: shadcn wall time 458 to 607 ms on CI between the Monday run and the latest run (+33%); locally 141 to 168 ms and 275 to 331 MiB (+19%).
28	
29	## Decisions (accepted)
30	
31	1. Object-literal members (shadcn `Icons.*`, +19): skip the extractor rule for now; count them separately in the harness.
32	2. Dependency re-exports (`export { TreeNode }`): keep ADR 0010 (never emitted). Ship only the narrow form where the project declares the binding (`const X = Ns.Member`, `const { Option } = Rc`).
33	3. "Vanilla" react-docgen: verify Storybook's real resolver configuration first; that is the headline, the other resolver is shown labelled.
34	4. Oracle headline: "agree of the whole universe"; "agree of listed" second; missing props reported apart.
35	5. Augmentation scan: do NOT pre-filter packages that do not list `react` (changes semantics; probable ADR). Dedupe resolution and parse lightly instead.
36	6. Dependency parse cache for warm runs: prototype on a throwaway branch and decide from the measurement (touches ADRs 0003, 0008, 0011).
37	7. NAPI TOON/slice view: yes, narrowly (one component slice) and last, after prop-level confidence exists.
38	8. Agent evaluation: deterministic only in CI. A model-in-the-loop mode, if ever, is manual.
39	Also: keep Storybook's default `htmlAttributes: full` (ADR 0024).
40	Release flow (trail 6): product package is `cargo/caliper-docgen` (npm `bin` cannot be an artifact product); attach CLI binaries; add build attestations. Verify these with the user before starting trail 6 (not yet answered).
41	
42	## Trails and branches
43	
44	Create each trail intent-only first (`entire trail create --no-branch --type task --title ... --body ...`), with the acceptance criteria below in the body. Then branches, PRs, links as in "Process".
45	
46	### Trail 1. Compare Caliper, RDT and react-docgen honestly
47	Acceptance: antd component recall about 95% with the new pairing (replayed 186/195 strict, 186/194 keeping today's any-call unwrap) and shadcn unchanged at 96.5% (none of its 55 unmatched are pairing cases); weekly.json records unmatched entries by cause and a `reference_version`, and `findings()` skips recall comparison across different reference versions; the oracle scores Caliper, RDT and react-docgen with the same rules and shows universe-based agree, missing by declaration stratum, react-docgen thrown files as their own column; Caliper's historical oracle numbers do not change.
48	Branches:
49	- `fix/weekly-pairing` (main). Files: `scripts/weekly.py`, `scripts/test_weekly.py`, `scripts/test_weekly_review.py`, `docs/measurement.md`. Same-file default aliases and `displayName`; unwrap `Object.assign`, `as`, `satisfies`, `!`, dotted wrappers, local alias chains; guards: the RDT name must be the file's or directory's own name, and a Caliper key an exact RDT entry already claims in the same file cannot be a pairing target (without them 5 wrong pairs appear). Cost: weekly script only, at most about 100 file reads per corpus.
50	- `feat/weekly-unmatched-record` (stacked on the above). Per-cause counts plus capped lists (about 30 KB for five corpora).
51	- `fix/weekly-caliper-key-collisions` (stacked, optional, +1 antd `splitter/Panel.tsx`).
52	- `oracle/function-marker-rule` (main). `apps/oracle/src/oracle-compare.ts`: optional or rest parameters cap every tool at "less precise" even if the tool kept the marker; rule becomes `(kp.optional && !cp.optional) || (kp.rest && !cp.rest)`. Caliper records neither marker so its numbers must not change.
53	- `oracle/tool-adapters` (stacked on the above). New `apps/oracle/src/tool-norm.ts`: RDT type object and react-docgen `tsType.raw` to the oracle's Norm form through one TS-string mapper. `scripts/rdt.mjs:31` currently keeps only the string "enum" for enum props (4 to 5% of own props); change it to keep the type object and only own props. react-docgen default resolver throws on 17 to 21% of files; record the failed count. Docs claim react-docgen reads files alone, but it follows relative imports (verified): fix the wording in `scripts/rdg.mjs` and `docs/measurement.md`. A scratch prototype of both adapters gave sensible verdicts on 27 fixture props.

Measured at main 53970b80 (parity harness, 110 shadcn and 84 antd sampled stories): props Storybook lists that we lack: shadcn 0, antd 14 in 2 stories (one verified defect: the rest probably a harness name collision); 14,795 of 14,800 shadcn extras are HTML attributes (deliberate; `htmlAttributes: none` cuts them to 5); shared props 338 and 1,315, same type text 58.3% and 67.4% (heuristic normaliser, about 68 and 160 unreviewed in "other"); real defects about 6% of shared props (defaults from dependency `defaultProps`, unresolved indexed access and `keyof typeof`, wrong `required`); degraded rate 4.8% and 4.0% (docs say 42.1% and 27.4% from 2026-10-24: not explained); antd, none attributes: 4.8% of prop instances are bare Named, 18 Opaque, 135 of 251 components carry an affecting diagnostic; TOON is about 7x smaller than canonical (antd 471 KB vs 3.4 MB) but has no NAPI route and drops provenance.
Branches:
- `feat/parity-detail-report` (main). `packages/storybook/scripts/storybook-parity.mjs`, `docs/storybook-parity.md`.
- `fix/trust-defects-batch` (main; run `just bench`). `crates/core/src/resolver/`, `pipeline/rdt.rs`: `PropsWithChildren<T>` children (Masonry), `keyof typeof` and `typeof X` in unions (Result.status, Cascader), indexed access on generic base-ui props, wrong `required` for an optional base and a required override (Segmented.options), collapse `undefined | boolean` to boolean, flag non-literal default expressions.
- `feat/prop-level-confidence` (main). `toon.rs`, `types/output.rs`, `crates/binding/src/`, `packages/napi/index.d.ts`: attach the degradation reason to the prop; TOON quotes literal unions, prints layer members and a source column; then the narrow NAPI slice view.
- `feat/agent-eval-weekly` (stacked after trail 1: it edits `weekly.py`). `scripts/agent_eval.py`, `scripts/agent_questions.json`, `scripts/test_agent_eval.py`.

### Trail 6. A complete release flow
Acceptance: each version produces one GitHub Release for `cargo/caliper-docgen` with notes; CLI binaries attached with build attestations; recovery through `callisto release pending` plus the drain job and a scheduled check; `callisto release --dry-run` in the PR check; the first real release verified from its receipt and the providers.
Facts: Callisto 0.16.0 (2026-10-28) is the latest and is what we pin. Our `callisto.toml` `publish-to` lists only crates.io and npm, so Callisto pushes tags and publishes packages but creates no GitHub Releases; `publish-to` accepts `"github-release"`; binaries need a `[release]` section (`product-package`, `forge-repository`, one `[[release.artifact]]` per target with `asset-name`); `release.yml` currently asserts zero artifact slots. Callisto's own worked example (`orin-dx/callisto` `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, 10 jobs against our 6) also has `recovery-checks` and `drain` jobs (`release pending`, finish the oldest unfinished release, then refresh the release PR), `actions/attest`, and a schedule trigger. Docs: `docs/releasing.md`, `docs/config.md` in that repo. A failed release is re-selected on every main push and holds back the release PR refresh. One run (the #274 push) failed at "Create or update the Callisto release PR" and recovered on the next push; cause not found. The tap reads tags and is unaffected.
Branches (stacked, all edit `release.yml` or `callisto.toml`): GitHub Releases with notes; binaries and attestations; recovery and schedule. Do not edit while a release is in flight.

## Order, sessions, concurrency

- Wave 0 (coordinator): create the six trails with the acceptance criteria above; write the branch table into each trail body; nothing else.
- Wave 1 in parallel: trail 1 and trail 2 (no shared files).
- Wave 2: trail 3 then trail 4 as one stacked lineage (serial); trail 5's independent branches once trail 1's weekly changes land; `agent-eval-weekly` last. Trail 6 after the in-flight release finishes.
- One session per trail. A session may fan out a workflow (isolated worktrees, schema'd results, an adversarial review stage) for independent branches; stacked branches are done in order. Agent teams are experimental and untried here: try one trail with a team before adopting.
- A coordinator session owns merge order, conflicts, the weekly rerun after merges and the trail bodies. Workers never merge or edit another trail.
- About three live sessions at most (separate `target` dirs, CPU contention; profiling must run alone).

## Process (rules that cost real incidents)

- Plan before create: trails and the branch table first, then branches. Do not create one trail per PR. A change cannot be reparented to another trail once it belongs to one (409), and the CLI has no delete.
- Link-first flow (recorded in memory `plan-trails-before-branches.md`): create the trail intent-only; push the branch; `entire trail link <n> --branch <b> --base <base>` (set `--base` to the parent branch for stacked branches, before any PR exists); Entire opens the PR; edit its title and body keeping the `entire-shadow-pr` marker. Linking a stacked branch after a PR already exists made Entire open a duplicate main-based PR (#277, #278); avoid.
- Merging: `entire trail merge` merges one change into its base through the trail's gates (approvals, CI, base CI, up to date) and never merges a trail's other changes; not yet tried here, test on a low-stakes PR. Merge stacks bottom-up; never merge a child into its parent's branch (that stranded #275's merge commit; the content was saved only because Entire's main-based duplicate #278 merged first). After a parent merges, retarget the child to `main` and merge `main` into it (no rebase, no force-push).
- Before any push run the whole CI set, not a subset of crates: `CI=1 CALIPER_TEST_TSC=<worktree>/apps/oracle/node_modules/typescript-beta/bin/tsc cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked`, `just lint doc-check typos machete`, and the TypeScript package tests if `packages/` changed. A missed CLI-crate literal broke #271 once. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in each worktree (snapshots need node_modules). Resolver changes also need `just bench` and a dependency-loaded shadcn run for time and RSS.
- Commits are GPG-signed (check `git log -1 --format='%h %G?'` prints G; use /usr/bin/git, one plain command per call, sandbox off for git writes). Never `--no-gpg-sign`, never force-push, never push to main.
- PR bodies: succinct, what changed, why, measured numbers, risks, the trail URL, the session URL last.
- Directly opened PRs use `gh pr create` (the global shim runs it as the PR bot and needs Touch ID; batch them). The global guard hook blocks commands that mention the bot's credentials; do not read `~/.config/orin-dx` or `~/Library/Application Support/OrinDX-PR-Bot`.
- Changesets: one short consumer paragraph, starting with the outcome; none for scripts-only changes.

## Tracking with Entire (from its help text; mostly untried)

- Worker start: `entire trail checkout <n> --worktree` then `entire trail resume <n>` (restores the checkpoint sessions on the trail branch and starts the agent with the trail's context).
- Coordinator: `entire session list`, `entire session tokens`, `entire trail watch <n>`, `entire dispatch`.
- Reviews: Entire's agent review runs on each PR; read it with `entire trail finding <repo>/<change> --project gh/orin-dx --freshness any --json`; the worker fixes verified findings. Findings, not comments, for agent feedback.
- Keep each trail body current with `entire trail update <n> --body ...` as branches land. Trail commands need the sandbox off (keychain and network).

## Unknowns to settle early

- Storybook's real react-docgen resolver configuration (decision 3).
- Why spectrum's oracle wrong-rate is 1.09% and shadcn's 0.08% (appeared between the baseline and the Monday run).
- Why the parity harness's degraded rate (4.8%, 4.0%) differs from the 2026-10-24 docs (42.1%, 27.4%).
- Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum behaviour for every new rule (not installed locally; use the CI weekly run on a branch).
- False-positive rate of every new detection rule except the 19 object-literal members measured.
- Release flow decisions for trail 6 (product package, binaries, attestations).

## Start prompts

Coordinator session:
> Read /Users/gabe/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md in full, then the memory note plan-trails-before-branches.md. You are the coordinator. Do Wave 0 only: create the six trails intent-only with the acceptance criteria and branch tables from the plan, confirm the trail numbers back to me, and wait. Do not create branches or PRs.

Worker session (replace N and the trail name):
> Read /Users/gabe/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md (the section for trail N and the Process section) and run `entire trail show N`. You own trail N only. Follow the plan's branch table, link-first flow and CI checklist. Fan out independent branches with a workflow in isolated worktrees; do stacked branches in order. Report numbers against the baselines in the plan. Update the trail body as branches land. Do not merge, and do not touch other trails' files.

1	# Caliper: plan for the next trails (written 2026-11-02)
2	
3	Read this whole file first. It is the agreed plan from a long planning session; the user approved the recommendations in "Decisions". Nothing in it has been created yet: no trail, no branch, no PR.
4	
5	## Goal
6	
7	What we care about, in order: (1) types that are accurate for Storybook's use and usable by in-process agents (monokl, no shell-out); (2) a comparison with RDT and react-docgen that is honest and repeatable; (3) speed, without breaking features; (4) a release flow that publishes GitHub Releases. Parity with RDT is a means, not the goal: the TypeScript 7.1 checker is the ground truth (it is also what Storybook's own component meta uses).
8	
9	## Where we are (main at 2daef927 when written)
10	
11	Merged this week: schema v4 (#266), detection by shape (#267, #270), on-demand checker hardening (#268), layer `members` and weekly recall columns (#271, #278), Chakra NonNullable (#272), terminal React builtins (#273), module augmentation (#274), Pick/keyof/union (#277). The release PR #269 merged; release run 41485334016 was in flight (do not edit `.github/workflows/release.yml` or `callisto.toml` until it ends).
12	
13	Weekly records (artifacts: weekly.json, weekly.md; `gh run download <id>` is read-only):
14	
15	| Run | Meaning |
16	| --- | --- |
17	| 41159666463 | baseline, main 240a61c9 |
18	| 41459968910 | Monday scheduled run, before the merges, main e2064d23 |
19	| 41479003541 | after the merges, main 53970b80 |
20	
21	Recall vs RDT (components / own flat / own with layers / @types/react), baseline to latest: mantine 85.9/100/-/99.2 to 89.1/100/100/99.6; chakra 79.4/100/-/99.4 to 92.5/100/100/99.4; shadcn 95.2/49.7/-/97.1 to 96.5/58.2/99.6/99.6; antd 64.0/86.4/-/91.9 to 79.7/86.4/99.3/99.1; spectrum 76.2/99.4/-/98.3 to 97.6/99.5/99.5/98.3. Component jumps come mostly from the harness (#275 excludes non-components and pairs exports), not from detection. Per-run RSS is now real (shadcn 334 MiB; the old 1,593 MiB was a measurement artifact).
22	
23	Speed vs RDT (CI): 17x to 58x faster, 2.6x to 6.8x less memory.
24	
25	Oracle (TS 7.1 checker, agree / wrong): mantine 90.9/0.00, chakra 100/0.00, shadcn 90.1/0.08, antd 93.1/0.00, spectrum 83.8/1.09 (new since baseline; present on the Monday run, so v4 or detection work, not the latest merges; cause not yet investigated).
26	
27	Regression: shadcn wall time 458 to 607 ms on CI between the Monday run and the latest run (+33%); locally 141 to 168 ms and 275 to 331 MiB (+19%).
28	
29	## Decisions (accepted)
30	
31	1. Object-literal members (shadcn `Icons.*`, +19): skip the extractor rule for now; count them separately in the harness.
32	2. Dependency re-exports (`export { TreeNode }`): keep ADR 0010 (never emitted). Ship only the narrow form where the project declares the binding (`const X = Ns.Member`, `const { Option } = Rc`).
33	3. "Vanilla" react-docgen: verify Storybook's real resolver configuration first; that is the headline, the other resolver is shown labelled.
34	4. Oracle headline: "agree of the whole universe"; "agree of listed" second; missing props reported apart.
35	5. Augmentation scan: do NOT pre-filter packages that do not list `react` (changes semantics; probable ADR). Dedupe resolution and parse lightly instead.
36	6. Dependency parse cache for warm runs: prototype on a throwaway branch and decide from the measurement (touches ADRs 0003, 0008, 0011).
37	7. NAPI TOON/slice view: yes, narrowly (one component slice) and last, after prop-level confidence exists.
38	8. Agent evaluation: deterministic only in CI. A model-in-the-loop mode, if ever, is manual.
39	Also: keep Storybook's default `htmlAttributes: full` (ADR 0024).
40	Release flow (trail 6): product package is `cargo/caliper-docgen` (npm `bin` cannot be an artifact product); attach CLI binaries; add build attestations. Verify these with the user before starting trail 6 (not yet answered).
41	
42	## Trails and branches
43	
44	Create each trail intent-only first (`entire trail create --no-branch --type task --title ... --body ...`), with the acceptance criteria below in the body. Then branches, PRs, links as in "Process".
45	
46	### Trail 1. Compare Caliper, RDT and react-docgen honestly
47	Acceptance: antd component recall about 95% with the new pairing (replayed 186/195 strict, 186/194 keeping today's any-call unwrap) and shadcn unchanged at 96.5% (none of its 55 unmatched are pairing cases); weekly.json records unmatched entries by cause and a `reference_version`, and `findings()` skips recall comparison across different reference versions; the oracle scores Caliper, RDT and react-docgen with the same rules and shows universe-based agree, missing by declaration stratum, react-docgen thrown files as their own column; Caliper's historical oracle numbers do not change.
48	Branches:
49	- `fix/weekly-pairing` (main). Files: `scripts/weekly.py`, `scripts/test_weekly.py`, `scripts/test_weekly_review.py`, `docs/measurement.md`. Same-file default aliases and `displayName`; unwrap `Object.assign`, `as`, `satisfies`, `!`, dotted wrappers, local alias chains; guards: the RDT name must be the file's or directory's own name, and a Caliper key an exact RDT entry already claims in the same file cannot be a pairing target (without them 5 wrong pairs appear). Cost: weekly script only, at most about 100 file reads per corpus.
50	- `feat/weekly-unmatched-record` (stacked on the above). Per-cause counts plus capped lists (about 30 KB for five corpora).
51	- `fix/weekly-caliper-key-collisions` (stacked, optional, +1 antd `splitter/Panel.tsx`).
52	- `oracle/function-marker-rule` (main). `apps/oracle/src/oracle-compare.ts`: optional or rest parameters cap every tool at "less precise" even if the tool kept the marker; rule becomes `(kp.optional && !cp.optional) || (kp.rest && !cp.rest)`. Caliper records neither marker so its numbers must not change.
53	- `oracle/tool-adapters` (stacked on the above). New `apps/oracle/src/tool-norm.ts`: RDT type object and react-docgen `tsType.raw` to the oracle's Norm form through one TS-string mapper. `scripts/rdt.mjs:31` currently keeps only the string "enum" for enum props (4 to 5% of own props); change it to keep the type object and only own props. react-docgen default resolver throws on 17 to 21% of files; record the failed count. Docs claim react-docgen reads files alone, but it follows relative imports (verified): fix the wording in `scripts/rdg.mjs` and `docs/measurement.md`. A scratch prototype of both adapters gave sensible verdicts on 27 fixture props.
54	- `oracle/three-tools-report` (stacked). `apps/oracle/src/oracle.ts` takes `--rdt` and `--rdg` dumps; `scripts/weekly.py` passes them; `entry['oracle']` keeps Caliper's `shared_props/agree/wrong` for continuity and adds `tools`. Cost about +5 to 15 s on the weekly Measure step (inferred). Edits `weekly.py`, so land the pairing branches first.
55	- Optional later: `oracle/default-and-description` (defaults and descriptions are not checker truth; label as such).
56	Known risks: rules validated only on antd and shadcn (Mantine, Chakra, Spectrum are not installed locally; validate from a CI weekly run on the branch); `excluded_sample` should be read on the other corpora; the 7.1 checker is a beta and some "wrong" verdicts may be the oracle's own (spectrum 1.09%).
57	
58	### Trail 2. Resolve faster with dependencies loaded
59	Acceptance: shadcn `--load-dependencies --no-cache` back to within 5% of the Monday numbers (141 ms, 275 MiB locally; weekly CI within 10% of the Monday record); extract output byte-identical; the watch and lazy tests in `crates/core/tests/react_augmentation_watch.rs` stay green; each branch states its measured delta.
60	Measured causes (local, shadcn, uncontended, median of 7 to 11; toggles disabled together restored 148 to 150 ms and 280 MiB): derived `Ord` on `Demand` sorts on the identical `from` path first (about 10 ms serial); module-only demands add resolution (about 10 ms) plus 64-file augmentation scans that parse and retain about 580 files (+50 MiB); the per-attribute-read `react_augmentations` lookup (77k calls per run, about 5.5 ms). `members` copying and JSON size are negligible (measured delta zero).
61	Branches:
62	- `perf/project-demands-sort` (main). `crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs`. Sort by (specifier, name) only. About 10 ms on shadcn, no RSS change.
63	- `perf/cache-react-augmentations` (main). `named_type_index.rs`, `resolver/html.rs`, `resolver/deps.rs`. Compute the augmenting-file list once per index layer chain and memoize per (react_file, key) inside the index (rebuilt per revision, never a static); record the file list as one slice and return early when the recorder already holds `reads_augmentations`. About 4 to 5 ms.
64	- `perf/module-demands-lean` (stacked on the sort branch; same file). Resolve module-only demands once per (specifier, nearest package.json directory), skip specifiers that resolve into the project, replace the full `parse_file` in `find_augmenting_files` with a light pass, retain nothing for files that are neither augmenting nor re-exporting. About 5 ms and -50 MiB. Do not pre-filter by package.json `react` dependency (decision 5).
65	- `perf/dependency-parse-cache` (throwaway prototype; decide from the numbers).
66	- `perf/members-shared-list`: skip (zero measured effect); hygiene only.
67	Hard constraint: Revision::affected_by (`pipeline/revision.rs` about lines 120 to 126) re-resolves a component when `change.react_namespace && depends_on.reads_augmentations` or the changed file is in `depends_on.files`; any caching must keep that true.
68	
69	### Trail 3. Detect components by shape and import source
70	Acceptance: `FC`, `ComponentType`, `FunctionComponent`, `Component`, `PureComponent` are matched through a `react` or `preact/compat` import under any alias or namespace (`R.FC`), and a same-named type from another module is not; `const Button = Inner` and `memo(Inner)` resolve even when `Inner` is declared later; exact-content tests; no precision regression; the 211 noise `SKIPPED_CANDIDATE` diagnostics (48 antd, 163 shadcn) go away.
71	Branches (stacked, same files):
72	- `fix/react-type-import-source` (main). `extractor/component.rs`, `extractor/mod.rs` (share one helper with `react_api` / `may_be_react`). Fixture-verified: 3 false negatives and 2 false positives, 0 hits in the corpora.
73	- `fix/alias-resolution-order` (stacked). Defer `try_rename_identifier_wrapped_component` to `finish()`; make the alias-variant matches in `resolver/html.rs` (about lines 83 to 87 and 128 to 132) and `resolver/callee.rs` (about 183 to 214) exhaustive.
74	
75	### Trail 4. Find the components we still miss
76	Acceptance: each new rule is by shape, never by library name; each has a precision sample (`scripts/precision-sample.py`, 25 per rule; the gate is 95%); every `SourceData` shape change appends fields at the end and bumps `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION` (ADR 0003), so the branches are strictly sequential; `just bench` and a dependency-loaded shadcn and Chakra measurement for time and peak RSS; object-literal members and dependency re-exports stay out (decisions 1 and 2).
77	Branches (one stack on trail 3's tip):
78	- `feat/imported-destructure-alias`. `const { Option } = Imported` and `const X = ImportedIdent` through the existing ImportedMemberAlias machinery; drop when it resolves to a project component of the same name. +1 antd, +4 shadcn (ChartLegend x4), and about 20 antd noise skips removed.
79	- `feat/factory-results`. `FunctionResult` for const-bound arrows with type parameters and for functions that return a rendering function; `return Local` with `Local = X as T`. +5 shadcn (IconLucide family), +1 antd (Calendar). DatePicker is not expected.
80	- `feat/cross-file-render-evidence`. Keep declined typed-props candidates; promote one when a project file imports and renders it. +1 antd (QRcodeStatus); shadcn `GET` must stay declined.
81	Known caution: the first analysis reported antd factory-built components as 6 real misses; only Calendar (+1) is expected to be recoverable. About 8 of the 55 shadcn misses are naming mismatches Caliper already covers (RDT `Tooltip` vs `ChartTooltip`): fix those in trail 1's pairing, not in the extractor.
82	
83	### Trail 5. Types Storybook and agents can trust
84	Acceptance: the parity report separates defects from deliberate differences; each verified defect has an exact-content test and the oracle agree rate does not fall; prop-level degradation reason is in canonical output (a new optional field is not a schema bump) and TOON; a 20-question deterministic agent evaluation runs in the weekly job and reports silent-wrong answers (issue when above 0 or when correct drops 5 points); a narrow NAPI slice view exists.
85	Measured at main 53970b80 (parity harness, 110 shadcn and 84 antd sampled stories): props Storybook lists that we lack: shadcn 0, antd 14 in 2 stories (one verified defect: the rest probably a harness name collision); 14,795 of 14,800 shadcn extras are HTML attributes (deliberate; `htmlAttributes: none` cuts them to 5); shared props 338 and 1,315, same type text 58.3% and 67.4% (heuristic normaliser, about 68 and 160 unreviewed in "other"); real defects about 6% of shared props (defaults from dependency `defaultProps`, unresolved indexed access and `keyof typeof`, wrong `required`); degraded rate 4.8% and 4.0% (docs say 42.1% and 27.4% from 2026-10-24: not explained); antd, none attributes: 4.8% of prop instances are bare Named, 18 Opaque, 135 of 251 components carry an affecting diagnostic; TOON is about 7x smaller than canonical (antd 471 KB vs 3.4 MB) but has no NAPI route and drops provenance.
86	Branches:
87	- `feat/parity-detail-report` (main). `packages/storybook/scripts/storybook-parity.mjs`, `docs/storybook-parity.md`.
88	- `fix/trust-defects-batch` (main; run `just bench`). `crates/core/src/resolver/`, `pipeline/rdt.rs`: `PropsWithChildren<T>` children (Masonry), `keyof typeof` and `typeof X` in unions (Result.status, Cascader), indexed access on generic base-ui props, wrong `required` for an optional base and a required override (Segmented.options), collapse `undefined | boolean` to boolean, flag non-literal default expressions.
89	- `feat/prop-level-confidence` (main). `toon.rs`, `types/output.rs`, `crates/binding/src/`, `packages/napi/index.d.ts`: attach the degradation reason to the prop; TOON quotes literal unions, prints layer members and a source column; then the narrow NAPI slice view.
90	- `feat/agent-eval-weekly` (stacked after trail 1: it edits `weekly.py`). `scripts/agent_eval.py`, `scripts/agent_questions.json`, `scripts/test_agent_eval.py`.
91	
92	### Trail 6. A complete release flow
93	Acceptance: each version produces one GitHub Release for `cargo/caliper-docgen` with notes; CLI binaries attached with build attestations; recovery through `callisto release pending` plus the drain job and a scheduled check; `callisto release --dry-run` in the PR check; the first real release verified from its receipt and the providers.
94	Facts: Callisto 0.16.0 (2026-10-28) is the latest and is what we pin. Our `callisto.toml` `publish-to` lists only crates.io and npm, so Callisto pushes tags and publishes packages but creates no GitHub Releases; `publish-to` accepts `"github-release"`; binaries need a `[release]` section (`product-package`, `forge-repository`, one `[[release.artifact]]` per target with `asset-name`); `release.yml` currently asserts zero artifact slots. Callisto's own worked example (`orin-dx/callisto` `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, 10 jobs against our 6) also has `recovery-checks` and `drain` jobs (`release pending`, finish the oldest unfinished release, then refresh the release PR), `actions/attest`, and a schedule trigger. Docs: `docs/releasing.md`, `docs/config.md` in that repo. A failed release is re-selected on every main push and holds back the release PR refresh. One run (the #274 push) failed at "Create or update the Callisto release PR" and recovered on the next push; cause not found. The tap reads tags and is unaffected.
95	Branches (stacked, all edit `release.yml` or `callisto.toml`): GitHub Releases with notes; binaries and attestations; recovery and schedule. Do not edit while a release is in flight.
96	
97	## Order, sessions, concurrency
98	
99	- Wave 0 (coordinator): create the six trails with the acceptance criteria above; write the branch table into each trail body; nothing else.
100	- Wave 1 in parallel: trail 1 and trail 2 (no shared files).
101	- Wave 2: trail 3 then trail 4 as one stacked lineage (serial); trail 5's independent branches once trail 1's weekly changes land; `agent-eval-weekly` last. Trail 6 after the in-flight release finishes.
102	- One session per trail. A session may fan out a workflow (isolated worktrees, schema'd results, an adversarial review stage) for independent branches; stacked branches are done in order. Agent teams are experimental and untried here: try one trail with a team before adopting.
103	- A coordinator session owns merge order, conflicts, the weekly rerun after merges and the trail bodies. Workers never merge or edit another trail.
104	- About three live sessions at most (separate `target` dirs, CPU contention; profiling must run alone).
105	
106	## Process (rules that cost real incidents)
107	
108	- Plan before create: trails and the branch table first, then branches. Do not create one trail per PR. A change cannot be reparented to another trail once it belongs to one (409), and the CLI has no delete.
109	- Link-first flow (recorded in memory `plan-trails-before-branches.md`): create the trail intent-only; push the branch; `entire trail link <n> --branch <b> --base <base>` (set `--base` to the parent branch for stacked branches, before any PR exists); Entire opens the PR; edit its title and body keeping the `entire-shadow-pr` marker. Linking a stacked branch after a PR already exists made Entire open a duplicate main-based PR (#277, #278); avoid.
110	- Merging: `entire trail merge` merges one change into its base through the trail's gates (approvals, CI, base CI, up to date) and never merges a trail's other changes; not yet tried here, test on a low-stakes PR. Merge stacks bottom-up; never merge a child into its parent's branch (that stranded #275's merge commit; the content was saved only because Entire's main-based duplicate #278 merged first). After a parent merges, retarget the child to `main` and merge `main` into it (no rebase, no force-push).
111	- Before any push run the whole CI set, not a subset of crates: `CI=1 CALIPER_TEST_TSC=<worktree>/apps/oracle/node_modules/typescript-beta/bin/tsc cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude caliper-docgen-napi --locked`, `just lint doc-check typos machete`, and the TypeScript package tests if `packages/` changed. A missed CLI-crate literal broke #271 once. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in each worktree (snapshots need node_modules). Resolver changes also need `just bench` and a dependency-loaded shadcn run for time and RSS.
112	- Commits are GPG-signed (check `git log -1 --format='%h %G?'` prints G; use /usr/bin/git, one plain command per call, sandbox off for git writes). Never `--no-gpg-sign`, never force-push, never push to main.
113	- PR bodies: succinct, what changed, why, measured numbers, risks, the trail URL, the session URL last.
114	- Directly opened PRs use `gh pr create` (the global shim runs it as the PR bot and needs Touch ID; batch them). The global guard hook blocks commands that mention the bot's credentials; do not read `~/.config/orin-dx` or `~/Library/Application Support/OrinDX-PR-Bot`.
115	- Changesets: one short consumer paragraph, starting with the outcome; none for scripts-only changes.
116	
117	## Tracking with Entire (from its help text; mostly untried)
118	
119	- Worker start: `entire trail checkout <n> --worktree` then `entire trail resume <n>` (restores the checkpoint sessions on the trail branch and starts the agent with the trail's context).
120	- Coordinator: `entire session list`, `entire session tokens`, `entire trail watch <n>`, `entire dispatch`.
121	- Reviews: Entire's agent review runs on each PR; read it with `entire trail finding <repo>/<change> --project gh/orin-dx --freshness any --json`; the worker fixes verified findings. Findings, not comments, for agent feedback.
122	- Keep each trail body current with `entire trail update <n> --body ...` as branches land. Trail commands need the sandbox off (keychain and network).
123	
124	## Unknowns to settle early
125	
126	- Storybook's real react-docgen resolver configuration (decision 3).
127	- Why spectrum's oracle wrong-rate is 1.09% and shadcn's 0.08% (appeared between the baseline and the Monday run).
128	- Why the parity harness's degraded rate (4.8%, 4.0%) differs from the 2026-10-24 docs (42.1%, 27.4%).
129	- Mantine, Chakra and Spectrum behaviour for every new rule (not installed locally; use the CI weekly run on a branch).
130	- False-positive rate of every new detection rule except the 19 object-literal members measured.
131	- Release flow decisions for trail 6 (product package, binaries, attestations).

You own trail N only. Follow the plan's branch table, link-first flow and CI checklist. Fan out independent branches with a workflow in isolated worktrees; do stacked branches in order. Report numbers against the baselines in the plan. Update the trail body as branches land. Do not merge, and do not touch other trails' files.

Create a repository-scoped project trail, then link its branch. In the current repository, publish the local branch first; no separate commit or push is required. Uses the current feature branch, or derives a new branch from the title when on the base branch. Use --branch to choose a branch, or --no-branch for intent only. With --no-branch, the current or --repo repository becomes the Trail scope and requires repository write access; --project without --repo creates unscoped intent instead. Repository writers can create scoped trails and link branches. Unscoped creation requires project management. With a branch, --idempotency-key applies only to linking; if linking fails, retry with trail link rather than creating another trail. With --repo, no local branch is published: link existing remote work or use --branch-action create to create it on the server from --base. This command does not commit changes or change the local checkout. Branches are preserved if creation fails.

Usage:
  entire trail create [flags]

Flags:
      --assignee strings         Assignee logins; replaces the complete list (--assignee= clears it)
      --base string              Base branch for new code work
      --body string              Trail description (--body= clears it on update)
      --branch string            Branch to use (defaults to the current feature branch; create derives one from the title on the base branch)
      --branch-action string     Branch action: link existing remote work, or create a new branch (default "link")
  -h, --help                     help for create
      --idempotency-key string   Retry key for linking a branch; with intent-only creation, requires project management
      --json                     Output raw JSON instead of a table
      --no-branch                Create intent scoped to the current or --repo repository; --project alone creates unscoped intent
      --priority string          Priority (urgent, high, medium, low, none)
      --status string            Lifecycle status (open, closed)
      --title string             Trail title
      --type string              Type (bug, feature, task)

Global Flags:
      --context name     Act as this saved login name for this command only — including the git and agent processes it spawns — instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
      --project string   Project as gh/<owner> or et/<project>; required for list, otherwise defaults to the repository's namespace
      --repo string      Target repository as forge/owner/repo (e.g. gh/acme/app) or a clone URL; for list, only filters the required --project
trail list requires --project gh/<owner> or et/<project>; --repo is only a filter within that project

cat > $D/t1.md <<'EOF'
## Goal
Compare Caliper, RDT and react-docgen honestly and repeatably. The TypeScript 7.1 checker is the ground truth.

## Acceptance criteria
- antd component recall about 95% with the new pairing (replayed 186/195 strict, 186/194 keeping today's any-call unwrap); shadcn unchanged at 96.5% (none of its 55 unmatched are pairing cases).
- weekly.json records unmatched entries by cause and a `reference_version`; `findings()` skips recall comparison across different reference versions.
- The oracle scores Caliper, RDT and react-docgen with the same rules and shows universe-based agree, missing by declaration stratum, and react-docgen thrown files as their own column.
- Caliper's historical oracle numbers do not change.

## Branches
| Branch | Base | Files / scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fix/weekly-pairing | main | scripts/weekly.py, test_weekly.py, test_weekly_review.py, docs/measurement.md. Same-file default aliases, displayName; unwrap Object.assign/as/satisfies/!/dotted wrappers/alias chains; guards against wrong pairs |
| feat/weekly-unmatched-record | fix/weekly-pairing (stacked) | per-cause counts plus capped lists (~30 KB for five corpora) |
| fix/weekly-caliper-key-collisions | stacked, optional | +1 antd splitter/Panel.tsx |
| oracle/function-marker-rule | main | apps/oracle/src/oracle-compare.ts: `(kp.optional && !cp.optional) \|\| (kp.rest && !cp.rest)`; Caliper numbers must not change |
| oracle/tool-adapters | oracle/function-marker-rule (stacked) | new apps/oracle/src/tool-norm.ts; scripts/rdt.mjs keeps type object and only own props; record react-docgen failed count; fix docs wording that react-docgen reads files alone |
| oracle/three-tools-report | stacked | oracle.ts takes --rdt/--rdg; weekly.py passes them; entry['oracle'] keeps Caliper fields, adds `tools`. Land pairing branches first (edits weekly.py) |
| oracle/default-and-description | optional, later | label defaults/descriptions as not checker truth |

## Risks
Rules validated only on antd and shadcn; validate Mantine/Chakra/Spectrum from a CI weekly run on the branch. The 7.1 checker is a beta; some "wrong" verdicts may be the oracle's own (spectrum 1.09%).

Plan: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md
EOF
cat > $D/t2.md <<'EOF'
## Goal
Resolve faster with dependencies loaded, without changing output.

## Acceptance criteria
- shadcn `--load-dependencies --no-cache` back within 5% of the Monday numbers (141 ms, 275 MiB locally; weekly CI within 10% of the Monday record).
- extract output byte-identical.
- watch and lazy tests in crates/core/tests/react_augmentation_watch.rs stay green.
- each branch states its measured delta.

## Measured causes (local, shadcn)
Derived `Ord` on `Demand` sorts on the identical `from` path first (~10 ms); module-only demands add resolution (~10 ms) plus 64-file augmentation scans that parse and retain ~580 files (+50 MiB); per-attribute-read `react_augmentations` lookup (77k calls, ~5.5 ms).

## Branches
| Branch | Base | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| perf/project-demands-sort | main | crates/core/src/dependency_types.rs: sort by (specifier, name); ~10 ms |
| perf/cache-react-augmentations | main | named_type_index.rs, resolver/html.rs, resolver/deps.rs: compute augmenting-file list once per index layer chain, memoize per (react_file, key) inside the index; ~4-5 ms |
| perf/module-demands-lean | perf/project-demands-sort (stacked) | resolve module-only demands once per (specifier, package.json dir), skip project-resolving specifiers, light pass instead of full parse_file; ~5 ms, -50 MiB. No pre-filter by package.json `react` |
| perf/dependency-parse-cache | throwaway prototype | decide from measurement (touches ADRs 0003, 0008, 0011) |
| perf/members-shared-list | skip | zero measured effect |

Hard constraint: Revision::affected_by (pipeline/revision.rs) must still re-resolve when `change.react_namespace && depends_on.reads_augmentations` or the changed file is in `depends_on.files`.

Plan: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md
EOF
cat > $D/t3.md <<'EOF'
## Goal
Detect components by shape and import source.

## Acceptance criteria
- `FC`, `ComponentType`, `FunctionComponent`, `Component`, `PureComponent` match through a `react` or `preact/compat` import under any alias or namespace (`R.FC`); a same-named type from another module does not.
- `const Button = Inner` and `memo(Inner)` resolve even when `Inner` is declared later.
- exact-content tests; no precision regression.
- the 211 noise SKIPPED_CANDIDATE diagnostics (48 antd, 163 shadcn) go away.

## Branches (stacked, same files)
| Branch | Base | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fix/react-type-import-source | main | extractor/component.rs, extractor/mod.rs; share one helper with react_api / may_be_react |
| fix/alias-resolution-order | fix/react-type-import-source (stacked) | defer try_rename_identifier_wrapped_component to finish(); make alias-variant matches in resolver/html.rs and resolver/callee.rs exhaustive |

Plan: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md
EOF
cat > $D/t4.md <<'EOF'
## Goal
Find the components Caliper still misses, by shape never by library name.

## Acceptance criteria
- each new rule has a precision sample (scripts/precision-sample.py, 25 per rule; gate 95%).
- every `SourceData` shape change appends fields at the end and bumps CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION (ADR 0003), so branches are strictly sequential.
- `just bench` plus dependency-loaded shadcn and Chakra measurement for time and peak RSS.
- object-literal members and dependency re-exports stay out.

## Branches (one stack on trail 3's tip)
| Branch | Base | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| feat/imported-destructure-alias | trail 3 tip | `const { Option } = Imported`, `const X = ImportedIdent` via ImportedMemberAlias; +1 antd, +4 shadcn, ~20 antd noise skips removed |
| feat/factory-results | previous (stacked) | FunctionResult for const-bound arrows with type params and render-function returns; +5 shadcn, +1 antd (Calendar) |
| feat/cross-file-render-evidence | previous (stacked) | promote a declined typed-props candidate when a project file imports and renders it; +1 antd; shadcn GET stays declined |

Caution: only Calendar is expected recoverable of antd factory-built components. ~8 of 55 shadcn misses are naming mismatches fixed in trail 1's pairing.

Plan: ~/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/plan/next-trails-2026-11-02.md
EOF
cat > $D/t5.md <<'EOF'
## Goal
Types Storybook and in-process agents can trust.

## Acceptance criteria
- parity report separates defects from deliberate differences; each verified defect has an exact-content test and oracle agree rate does not fall.
- prop-level degradation reason in canonical output (new optional field, not a schema bump) and TOON.

- a narrow NAPI slice view exists.

## Branches

| --- | --- | --- |
| feat/parity-detail-report | main | packages/storybook/scripts/storybook-parity.mjs, docs/storybook-parity.md |
| fix/trust-defects-batch | main (run just bench) | resolver/, pipeline/rdt.rs: PropsWithChildren<T> children, keyof typeof / typeof X in unions, indexed access on generic base-ui props, wrong `required` (Segmented.options), undefined\|boolean, non-literal defaults |
| feat/prop-level-confidence | main | toon.rs, types/output.rs, crates/binding/src, packages/napi/index.d.ts: degradation reason on prop; TOON literal unions, layer members, source column; then narrow NAPI slice view |
| feat/agent-eval-weekly | stacked after trail 1 (edits weekly.py) | scripts/agent_eval.py, agent_questions.json, test_agent_eval.py |

EOF
